info.description:
**Weekly soil-water-stress outlook for a point location, aimed at oil-palm plantations.**
Think "Open-Meteo, but for plantation water stress".

> **INDICATIVE, NOT VALIDATED.** Every number is model-derived from gridded weather data. Nothing here
> has been checked against field observations; the class cut-offs (0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 of plant-available
> water) have *no citable source*. This is not a yield forecast and makes no savings claim. Every
> response repeats this in its `meta` block.

## Quick start
```
curl "https://YOUR-HOST/v1/outlook?lat=-2.79&lon=104.60&days=7"
```
Examples in curl, JavaScript and Python are in the project README (`docs/EXAMPLES.md`).

## Endpoints
* `GET /v1/forecast`: normalised daily rain, ET0, temperature.
* `GET /v1/water-balance`: daily soil-water deficit and stress (FAO-56 style single bucket).
* `GET /v1/outlook`: Low / Moderate / High / Critical per day plus a summary (**start here**).
* `GET /health`: liveness.

## Authentication
Demo mode is open. If the operator sets API keys, send `X-API-Key: <key>` on every `/v1` request
(401 without a valid key).

## Errors (JSON `{"detail": "..."}`)
| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Missing/invalid API key | Send `X-API-Key` |
| 422 | Invalid input (e.g. latitude outside -90..90). Body is a list of field errors | Fix the parameter |
| 429 | **You** exceeded the rate limit (per minute). `Retry-After` header = seconds | Wait, then retry |
| 502 | Weather provider failed (timeout, server error, bad data) | Retry shortly |
| 503 | Weather provider is rate-limiting **us**. `Retry-After` header = seconds | Wait, then retry |

## Stale data
If the weather provider is down and a cached answer (up to 48 h old by default, labelled stale) or a committed last-good snapshot for the demo site exists, it is served
with `meta.weather_stale = true`, `meta.weather_age_seconds`, a `STALE WEATHER` line in
`meta.assumptions`, and the response header `X-ClimSmart-Data: stale; age=<seconds>s`.

## Weather data and licence
Weather: [Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com), CC BY 4.0. **The free Open-Meteo tier is
non-commercial only.** Show the attribution text from `meta.sources`.

Cost-benefit view of APSIM-X management scenarios for **Mambang Muda only** (other points: 404). APSIM-X was run offline for: the founder's N fertiliser (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x), the same N in 6 doses instead of 3, and a rule-based irrigation top-up (the founder's file has an Irrigation model but nothing applies water; we add a simple trigger rule). For each scenario versus base the response gives delta FFB (t/ha/yr), delta revenue, delta fertiliser cost, delta water cost, net difference, a +/-`sensitivity_pct` price sensitivity, a yield-response what-if, break-even FFB price and break-even yield factor, and the change in N leaching (APSIM output, no money value). All formulas are in `formulas`. `weather=rain_scaled` re-reads the same scenarios with rain scaled to the station. **Indicative, NOT VALIDATED: no Sumatra calibration, palm planting year ASSUMED 2012, one point. No savings, profit or ROI claim is made.** Leaching prevention: the model has no dedicated practice; leaching is reported as an output and only N rate/splitting change it.

formulas: d_ffb_t_ha = FFB_scenario - FFB_base   (APSIM-X, mean of the full hindcast years)
d_extra_harvest_haul_cost = d_ffb_t_ha * harvest_haul_cost_per_tonne   (0 unless you set it)
d_water_cost = (irrigation_mm_scenario - irrigation_mm_base) * 10 m3 per mm per ha * water_price_per_m3
d_irrigation_fixed_cost = fixed cost if the scenario irrigates (mm > 0) minus the same for the base
net_difference = d_revenue - d_extra_harvest_haul_cost - d_fertiliser_cost - d_water_cost - d_irrigation_fixed_cost
break_even_ffb_price = harvest_haul_cost + (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) / d_ffb   (price at which net = 0; undefined when d_ffb = 0)

break_even_yield_factor f: net(f) = f * d_ffb * (ffb_price - harvest_haul_cost) - (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) = 0  ->  f = (d_fert + d_water + d_fixed) / (d_ffb * (ffb_price - harvest_haul_cost)); f = 1 means APSIM-X's response as simulated
sensitivity 'unfavourable': FFB price x (1 - p), all cost prices x (1 + p); 'favourable': the reverse; p = sensitivity_pct/100
yield what-if: d_ffb multiplied by (1 - w), 1, (1 + w) with w = yield_whatif_pct/100; an illustration of a wrong response, NOT an error estimate

limitations: INDICATIVE, NOT VALIDATED: the APSIM-X oil-palm model has not been calibrated or checked against any observation for this site or for Sumatra (the founder's model notes say BunchSizeMax was fitted to Papua New Guinea data and RUE follows Henson & Dolmat 2003).
Only the Mambang Muda point is supported: there is no APSIM run for any other location.

Palm age is an assumption, not the estate's: the founder's file plants on 2001-01-01, but run past about 2021 the model breaks (palms 25 years old: leaf area goes negative and APSIM aborts). The copy used here plants on 1 January of an assumed year (default 2012, so about 14.8 years old in Oct 2026) and starts the clock that day. Real block ages, density and management are unknown.

Soil provenance is undocumented: layer values look partly measured and partly template defaults; a single 2 m profile represents the whole point; initial water and nitrate in 2001 look implausible (spun up since).

Weather: history 2000-2022 is a nearby station series (about 8-9 km away, source undocumented); 2023 onward is an Open-Meteo model grid cell. The two sources differ (see weather_inputs.overlap_check), so the splice can shift the water balance. Forecast days use forecast rainfall, which is uncertain.
Free Open-Meteo tier is non-commercial; this is a demo.

The class on APSIM numbers is taken from APSIM's water-stress index (1 - fw) using the same provisional 0.3/0.5/0.7 cut-offs as the simple bucket (no citable source). It is a different quantity from the bucket's soil depletion: in the model fw = palm transpiration / demand, and transpiration is limited to a supply rate (sum over layers of KL x (soil water - LL15), about 3.5 mm/day in Aug 2026), so fw falls below 1 on high-demand days even when the soil is wetter than field capacity.
Not a yield forecast. The model reports FFB yield in its annual outputs but that is not served or claimed.

get.description: Runs a transparent single-layer FAO-56 style soil-water bucket over a spin-up period (`spinup_days` of recent past, starting from a full store unless `initial_depletion_mm` is set) and then the forecast. Returns the daily deficit (mm), stress coefficient `ks` and water fluxes. Crop and soil defaults (115 mm per 1 m root zone, Kc 1.0, p 0.65) are literature-based and **provisional**: see `meta.parameter_sources`; override them with query parameters. **Indicative, not validated; not a yield forecast.**
